rule: Every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N (one-to-one relationship)
rationale: S_N is designated as a one-to-one join key with Acc_Info_dirty.S_N. Referential integrity must be enforced to ensure all customer bio records have corresponding account info records.

rule: Account_No must be exactly 4 digits
rationale: Account numbers are 4-digit identifiers ranging from 1001-1028. Values must conform to 4-digit format after conversion to string.

rule: Account_No must be unique across records
rationale: Evidence shows 2 duplicate account numbers (1001, 1010) appearing in 4 records total. While duplicates may represent valid business scenarios, they require verification and should be flagged for review.

rule: Name must be in Title Case format (excluding lowercase particles like bin, binte, s/o, d/o)
rationale: 28 of 30 values use Title Case. One value is all lowercase ('lim wei jie') and one is all uppercase ('WANG SHI JIE'), requiring standardization to match the dominant pattern.

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: Name particles indicating gender must match the Gender column: Bin/s/o indicate Male; Binte/d/o indicate Female
rationale: Malay and Indian naming conventions use specific particles to indicate gender and lineage. 'Bin' and 's/o' (son of) indicate male; 'Binte' and 'd/o' (daughter of) indicate female. Mismatches suggest data entry errors.

check_params.logic: (re.search(r'\b(Bin|s/o)\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'male') or (re.search(r'\b(Binte|d/o)\b', str(row['Name']), re.IGNORECASE) and str(row['Gender']).strip().lower() != 'female')

rule: ID_No must follow Singapore NRIC/FIN format: one prefix letter (S, T, F, or G), followed by 7 digits, ending with one uppercase checksum letter
rationale: 93.3% of values conform to the standard 9-character format (e.g., S1234567D). Two records deviate: '1916569C' lacks the prefix letter, and 'F212233V' has only 6 digits instead of 7.

rule: ID_No must be unique across records
rationale: National identification numbers should uniquely identify individuals. Evidence shows duplicate value 'F1011121T' appearing in 2 records, requiring verification.

rule: Race must be one of: Chinese, Malay, Indian
rationale: All 30 records contain one of three semantic categories (Chinese, Malay, Indian) but with case variations. Values outside this set indicate invalid data entry.

rule: Gender must be either Male or Female
rationale: Field contains four observed values representing two categories with case inconsistencies. Only 'Male' and 'Female' (Title Case) are valid canonical values.

rule: Age must be parseable as a numeric value
rationale: Column is intended as int64 but contains one text representation 'Twenty-five' (3.3% of records) that cannot be parsed as numeric.

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 years inclusive
rationale: Age represents human lifespan. Values outside 0-120 are biologically implausible. Observed range includes negative values (-5) which violate this constraint.

rule: Age must be at least 13 years for service accounts
rationale: Evidence flags 2 records with ages below 13 (-5 and 4) as potentially unrealistic for a consumer service, suggesting data entry errors or test accounts requiring verification.

rule: Contact_No must not be null
rationale: Contact number is a mandatory contact field with 2 missing values (6.7% of records) that require completion for customer communication.

rule: Contact_No must be a valid Singapore phone number with 8 digits (with or without +65 prefix)
rationale: All numbers appear to be Singapore-based. Valid Singapore phone numbers have exactly 8 digits. One value '8964359' has only 7 digits and appears truncated.

rule: Email must contain exactly one @ symbol with no whitespace
rationale: 4 records (13.3%) contain structurally malformed emails: 'not-an-email' and 'useremail.com' lack @, 'zx91 @example.com' contains space, 'nabilah@@example.com' has double @.

rule: Country must be standardized to 'Singapore'
rationale: All 8 observed distinct values represent Singapore in various formats (SG, S'pore, Singapura, 新加坡, etc.). Standardization to the canonical English form 'Singapore' is required.

rule: Street_Name must be in Title Case format
rationale: 29 of 30 values use Title Case. One value 'HOLLAND ROAD' appears in all caps, deviating from the dominant pattern and requiring standardization.

check_params.logic: any(w[0].islower() or w.isupper() for w in str(row['Street_Name']).split() if len(w) > 1)

rule: Postal_Code must be exactly 6 digits when represented as string
rationale: Singapore postal codes are 6-digit identifiers. Observed values include 4-digit (6907) and 5-digit (99999) codes that do not conform to the standard format.

rule: ID_No must match the corresponding ID value in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: Both tables contain national identification numbers for the same customers (Cust_Bio_dirty.ID_No and Acc_Info_dirty.ID). These must be identical for matching S_N values to ensure identity consistency across tables.

check_params.semantic_check: ID_No must exactly match ID for the same S_N

rule: Name must correspond to Full_Name in Acc_Info_dirty for the same S_N (accounting for formatting variations)
rationale: Both tables contain customer names (Cust_Bio_dirty.Name and Acc_Info_dirty.Full_Name). While formatting may vary (e.g., 'Danish' vs 'Danish Bin Kamaruddin', case differences), the names should represent the same individual for matching S_N values.

check_params.semantic_check: Name must match Full_Name accounting for case differences, name particles, and abbreviations

rule: S_N must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty (one-to-one join key)
rationale: One-to-one key relationship detected by MinHash analysis; duplicate values break the join.

rule: Email must be unique within Cust_Bio_dirty
rationale: Column is 96.7% distinct with duplicate value(s) ['thm@example.com'] observed; treated as a candidate identifier — duplicates flagged for review.
